lesson_content: Identify six bird species by comparing multiple visible field marks, not color alone. A male mallard has a glossy green head, yellow bill, and white neck ring. A male green-winged teal has a chestnut head and green eye patch. A rock pigeon has a gray body, two dark wing bars, and an iridescent neck. A Canada goose has a long black neck, white chinstrap, and brown body. A mute swan has a white body, long curved neck, and orange bill with a black base. A male northern cardinal has red plumage, a pointed crest, and a black face mask around a stout orange-red bill. Compare the pictured examples and preserve uncertainty when field marks are unclear. All six species are taught; the independent test also asks students to recall the mallard's bill color without a picture.
